body:
## Why

Follow-up to #100. With `WindowCommandPolicy::ApplicationOwned` a manually mounted view may *issue* window commands, but the command pump resolves them against a native-window registry that only `ScriptApplication::run` populates — a host that owns the top-level window and mounts via `PreparedScriptView::mount` starts empty, so `ctx.close_window("main")` fails with `native window `main` is unavailable`. Hit by disktree-rhai's `q` key.

## What

- `ScriptViewHandle::register_native_window(id, window, cx)` — inserts the host's `AnyWindowHandle` under `id` in the mounted view's registry (re-register replaces; dispose removes). One call after `mount`, mirroring what `ScriptApplication::run` does internally.
- No behavior change for `run`-based apps.

## Verification

`cargo test -p gpui-rhai --lib` green (446), clippy clean. The crate has no window-level test harness; end-to-end behavior verified in the downstream app (disktree-rhai `q` now closes its window — blind-tested via wtype + process check).
title: feat(app): let manual hosts register their native window
